builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free Co-Evolution of an LLM Agent
summary: Replaces hand-written system-prompt policies and teacher-model distillation with on-demand skill files that the model itself extends from deployment logs, gated by code checks and self-review, plus GRPO LoRA training on logged conversations. Costs a RL training pipeline (GRPO with LoRA, feasible on a single 24 GB GPU for 12B-scale models only with careful memory management), a validation-gate infrastructure for rule admission, and logged task outcomes; latency impact is small since skills are retrieved on demand. Can fail when deployment logs lack reference outcomes, when self-written rules pass the gates but encode wrong policy, and because gains were shown only on two tau2-bench domains and may not transfer.
rationale: The recipe is reproducible on constrained infrastructure (LoRA, no teacher model), but its value depends on having logged outcomes and a domain where self-curated rules are verifiable, so it warrants a small-scale pilot rather than immediate adoption.
technique: Teacher-free skill curation plus GRPO LoRA co-evolution

claims.statement: Replaces hand-written system-prompt policies and teacher-model distillation with on-demand skill files that the model itself extends from deployment logs, gated by code checks and self-review, plus GRPO LoRA training on logged conversations. Costs a RL training pipeline (GRPO with LoRA, feasible on a single 24 GB GPU for 12B-scale models only with careful memory management), a validation-gate infrastructure for rule admission, and logged task outcomes; latency impact is small since skills are retrieved on demand. Can fail when deployment logs lack reference outcomes, when self-written rules pass the gates but encode wrong policy, and because gains were shown only on two tau2-bench domains and may not transfer.
After two rounds, +12.5 and +19.5 pass^1 points (retail, airline) and +18.4/+22.0 pass^4 over the 12B baseline on tau2-bench, exceeding the full-policy reference agent by 11.8/8.0 pass^1.
